minor.issue: Returns 200 for unknown column IDs instead of the spec-required 404. Root cause: in routes/account_volume_grid.py delete_column(), the update sets `$set: {updated_at: now}` alongside `$pull`, so mongo's modified_count is >0 even when the $pull matched nothing — the `if res.modified_count == 0: 404` guard never triggers. Fix: pre-check with a find_one for the column id in config.columns, OR drop the $set updated_at from the same call and rely purely on $pull's array modification. Reproduce: `curl -X DELETE $URL/api/account-volume-grid/columns/nope-id` → 200 {"deleted":true}.

action_items: Fix DELETE /api/account-volume-grid/columns/{id} to return 404 for unknown ids (either split the $pull and $set updated_at into two ops with a pre-check, or use a find_one guard before update_one).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/account_volume_grid.py delete_column: `modified_count==0` check is defeated by co-located `$set updated_at`; unknown ids silently succeed (see backend_issues.minor above).

PUT /rows/{account_id} `custom_values` is merged via {**existing, **payload} — no validation that the payload keys correspond to defined custom column ids. A stale/deleted column id from the client can still write arbitrary keys into account.volume_grid_values and remain there after the column is deleted, effectively creating orphan data. Consider filtering by known column ids from volume_grid_config, or purging keys on column delete.

Frontend evalFormula uses `new Function(...)` on a regex-guarded expression. The guard `/^[0-9+\-*/(). NaN]*$/` (after stripping NaN) is safe for the shipped column names, but any future custom-column name containing operator characters could inject an expression. Consider a proper mini-parser or shunting-yard for math evaluation.

Frontend column-name resolution in formulaContext uses `expr.split(name).join(...)` — this is a substring replace, so a column named 'Volume' would also match inside 'Expected Monthly Volume'. The sort-by-length-desc partially mitigates but doesn't fully protect. Word-boundary tokenization would be safer.

Backend does not enforce RBAC on POST/DELETE /columns or PUT /rows — any authenticated user (including non-admin/sales roles) can add/delete tenant-wide columns. If Volume Tracking is admin/sales-only per Sales module gating, add a role check on the mutating routes.

rca of the issue: DELETE /api/account-volume-grid/columns/{column_id} unknown-id bug: the endpoint issues one update_one({tenant_id}, {$pull:{columns:{id:column_id}}, $set:{updated_at:now}}). MongoDB counts the $set as a modification of the parent config doc regardless of whether $pull matched, so update_result.modified_count is 1 and the code returns {deleted:true}. Mitigation: (a) before the update, `col = await db[CONFIG].find_one({tenant_id, 'columns.id': column_id})` and raise 404 if None; OR (b) inspect the array before/after via a two-step read-then-update; OR (c) drop the redundant `$set updated_at` in this call and use only $pull — then modified_count truly reflects whether an element was removed.
